item.title: This year's MacArthur Fellows include researchers who fuse science and justice
item.description: The MacArthur Foundation has just announced its latest batch of 20 fellows. Among the recipients of the $800,000 "no-strings-attached" fellowships are researchers who were recognized for their work at the intersection of science and justice.
item.content:encoded:
The MacArthur Foundation has just announced its latest batch of 20 fellows. Among the recipients of the $800,000 "no-strings-attached" fellowships are researchers who were recognized for their work at the intersection of science and justice.

(Image credit: The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation)
item.dc:creator: Ari Daniel

item.title: Meet the 20 scholars and artists who've just won MacArthur Fellowships
item.description: A historian who studies wage gaps between races and a saxophonist whose live performances include a chef are among the latest recipients of the philanthropic group's annual, no-strings-attached $800,000 grants.
item.content:encoded: A historian who studies wage gaps between races and a saxophonist whose live performances include a chef are among the latest recipients of the philanthropic group's annual, no-strings-attached $800,000 grants.

item.title: The Trump administration weakens fuel efficiency standards for new cars
item.description: The Trump administration says easing these standards will make cars more affordable. Critics say it's not so simple and could be costly for the environment.

item.title: SpaceX's Starship launches on first orbital mission from Texas
item.description: Starship is key to SpaceX's commercial success and NASA's plans to land humans on the moon. This is the 14th flight of the uncrewed Starship, but the first time it reached orbit.

item.description: D.C.'s Rat Rangers take anyone who is interested on night time safaris through some of the Capitol's filthiest back alleys to learn the way of the rats, and to be better humans.

item.title: Mexico's Baja California braces for Hurricane Polo as Hurricane Nolo threatens Hawaii
item.description: Hurricane Nolo edged further away from the Hawaiian Islands on Sunday as major Hurricane Polo bore down on Mexico's Baja California peninsula with a threat of storm surge, high winds and heavy rains.

item.title: We're looking for life on other planets. Are we ready to find it?
item.description: In 1960, astronomer Frank Drake listened for signals from alien worlds. Reporter Brendan Byrne's podcast When We Find Them picks up the search and asks what would happen if we finally find something.

item.title: The hot spot: World Sauna Congress convenes in Oslo as global interest skyrockets
item.description: At the World Sauna Congress in Oslo, NPR's Will Stone covers how scientists and enthusiasts are exploring heat exposure as a growing global trend to boost wellbeing and fight social isolation.

item.title: The Pacific is churning with hurricanes. The Atlantic is quiet. Blame El Niño
item.description: The Pacific Ocean has had an unusual number of storms this year, while the Atlantic hasn't recorded a single full-blown hurricane. Scientists point to an exceptionally strong El Niño.
item.content:encoded:
